A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE reconstruction, retrieval, latent-intrusion, and human interpretability results, with additional experiments in Appendices C–F.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a neuron-based interpretability comparison, runtime measurements, and a retrieval-failure case study in Appendices G–I.

M1.justification: The BatchTopK SAE, reconstruction objective, latent descriptions, IDF weighting, and CL-SR indexing and scoring procedures are unchanged. The revised introduction to Section 5 clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MSMARCO, TREC DL 2019/2020, TREC-COVID, and NFCorpus. The added comparisons and failure example reuse existing retrieval and interpretability coverage without introducing a new dataset or task population.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds raw SimLM neurons as an intrusion-test comparator, and Appendix H adds SimLM to the efficiency comparison. Table 4's SPLADE-max label clarifies the existing SPLADE v2 (max) baseline; DistilSPLADE and SPLADE v3 are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces encoding and search latency measurements using CPU/GPU implementations, batch size 1, and all 6,980 MSMARCO Dev queries. These supplement v1's FLOPs, active-document-length, and storage measurements; existing training and evaluation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a targeted test of interpretability against raw embedding dimensions. Appendix I and Table 13 add a SimLM retrieval-failure analysis. Existing IDF ablations, latent-count sensitivity analyses, and mismatch tests remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly reports three passes through the timing evaluation and selection of the lowest observed latency, without uncertainty intervals. Existing variance and significance reporting is unchanged; no increase in repetitions of the original experiments is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 retain their numerical results. Appendix G adds raw-neuron accuracy of 0.46 against SAE accuracy of 0.86, rounding the retained 0.859. Table 12 adds timings, including CPU search latencies of 924.42 ms/query for SimLM and 117.96 for CL-SR Efficient; Table 13 adds failure-case activation values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses, and retrieval equations are unchanged, and neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. Appendix G's rotation-invariance discussion provides conceptual motivation rather than a new derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: SAE-based interpretation of dense retrieval and efficient, interpretable concept-level sparse retrieval robust to vocabulary and semantic mismatches. The additions support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds a rationale for learning an interpretable basis instead of interpreting individual dimensions. Appendix I attributes a retrieval failure to misleading immune-system overlap and missing virus-specific overlap. The existing limitations discussion is retained.

D1.justification: Appendix H documents PyTorch/GPU and NumPy/CPU timing implementations, an RTX 3090, an Intel i7-14700KF, and the timing setup. v2 also explicitly identifies the existing SPLADE baseline as non-distilled. Original training details, prompts, and code-access information remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lassance et al. (2024), Li et al. (2022), Olah et al. (2020), and Zhan et al. (2021). These support a limited expansion explaining the SPLADE baseline choice, timing implementation, and positioning against neuron-based interpretation.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendices G–I, acknowledgments, a baseline-selection paragraph, and small wording refinements. The main narrative, section sequence, and existing appendix explanations are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the efficiency table and failure-case table as Tables 12 and 13. Figure 3 and several existing appendix displays are repositioned, while the original figures and table structures are retained apart from the SPLADE row-label clarification.

improvement.justification: The raw-neuron control, measured runtimes, and concrete failure diagnosis in Appendices G–I strengthen evidence that v1 supported mainly through SAE comparisons, efficiency proxies, and successful examples. These are useful, targeted gains. Minimum-of-three timing summaries without uncertainty and a single illustrative failure analysis limit their evidential strength, supporting a modest overall improvement.
